about: The procedural world's numbers (B01, D-game-34). vertical is the range of block rows (y -64 to 320, whole 16-block chunk layers) and the sea level, which stays 32 so the valley keeps its coordinates. climate gives the six smooth fields the world is made of, each a fractal of gradient noise (cell is the first octave's size in blocks, each octave halves it; warpBlocks bends the field by that many blocks at most) sampled every latticeBlocks blocks and interpolated; temperature falls by lapsePer100Blocks thousandths for every 100 blocks above the sea, and snow and trees follow that value against the thresholds in altitude. height holds three splines (points are [input, output]; an input is thousandths of the field's range): base from the continentalness (blocks), rangeFactor from the erosion (thousandths: how much of the peaks shows) and peaks from the ridges (blocks), so height = base + factor x peaks + hills; above softCapAbove the ground rises at half rate and never passes clamp. Terraces shape the steep middle slopes, crags the highest ridges, rivers are carved where the river field is near zero down to bedHeight (below the sea) and lakes pull low calm basins down to theirs. Every number is a whole number: lengths are blocks, field values thousandths of their range (-1000 to 1000). Biomes are in biomes.json; no word of Spanish belongs here. regionBlend (B06) is how the land outside an authored region (the valley) is eased into its edge: over margin blocks the ground eases to the edge's height, no trunk stands within treeClearance columns of the border and the trees thin across the margin, the continentalness never falls below a floor that runs from landBias.floor at the edge to landBias.shoreFloor at landBias.radius blocks out (so no sea opens at the valley's feet), the edge's own roughness is blurred over edgeSmoothing.blurRadius columns and the ground eases from the edge's exact height to the blurred one over edgeSmoothing.ease blocks (so the edge does not comb the land into ridges), and each exit corridor is a road of halfWidth blocks each side of the line from (fromX, fromZ) to (toX, toZ), its bank easing over shoulder blocks and giving way to the land over the last fade blocks. Field values are thousandths; every number is a whole number. B02b and its redo (the owner's map reviews of B02): climate.continents makes the continentalness continents, not noise: the plane is cut into jittered cells (cell blocks wide), each block of seaBlock x seaBlock cells holds seaPerBlock open-sea cells (so the sea is 35 to 45% of any 16k square), the rest are land, and a channel of sea (between channelMin and channel blocks each side, varied by a noise of widthCell) runs along every border, so the land cells are continents 5 000 to 15 000 blocks across and the sea is one connected ocean whatever the seed; the coast is bent by two warps (the continentalness's own and coastCell/coastBlocks); the continentalness is the signed distance from the coast (scaleBlocks blocks make 1 000 thousandths) and salt picks the arrangement (23 gives the three maps of the review about 40% sea). The base spline falls from y 32 at the shore to y -58 far out (a long shelf) and rises steeply to a flat clean beach strip, then gently over wide plains and inland to about y 90; height.coast fades the peaks out over the land near the sea (peaksFrom to peaksTo), calms the hills there (hillsFrom to hillsTo, hillsFloor) and takes them off the low ground (flatFrom to flatTo) so no speckle of flats and pools lies just over the sea. The ridges are one octave (a ridge line is a chain) with rounded crests (round), the erosion a wide field (cell 12288) so chains run for thousands of blocks, the peaks spline is steep at the top, peakVariation scales the peaks along a range so the spine rises to summits and falls to saddles, and the crags are big. The rivers: the river field's zero lines are valleys cut into the ground; rivers.valley says from what height (from) the floor stays about as deep under the ground as there (depthGrowth deeper with height) and how much the valley widens with the height (widthPer10Blocks), the river is faded out from fadeFromHeight to fadeToHeight (its sources, in the ranges), and the water stands only where the floor is under the sea, which the floor keeps for the lower reach (waterFrom to waterTo continentalness): the water is the sea's level, so higher up a valley is dry. The lakes are inland basins just beyond the shore. regionBlend: landBias pulls the continentalness up round a region (floor to shoreFloor over radius blocks) so no sea is within 1 000 blocks of the valley, landBias.erosion keeps the ring round it calm (to fromRadius) and makes a belt of rugged land from toRadius to fadeRadius where ranges stand, headwater.distance is how many blocks beyond the blend margin a river's valley shallows to nothing and a lake shrinks to a pond; inside the margin there is no river or lake.
